title: Finite-cover connectedness criterion for etale module sections
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume that for every finite morphism $h:X\prime\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and every irreducible closed subset $C\subseteq X\prime$, the intersection $C\cap h^{-1}(i(Z))$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. For every commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], the canonical inverse-image restriction [def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback] $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}F)$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules.

source.place: Lemma 59.82.2; spectral input at Tag 09ZG, Lemma 59.82.4

proof.text: Forget the scalar action on F, obtaining an abelian etale sheaf G. Apply the abelian finite-cover connected-intersection criterion to i, hconn and G. In the definition of globalSectionsUpperStarMap, the factors before and after the adjunction-unit evaluation are isomorphisms. Cancel them to conclude that the abelian adjunction unit evaluated at the terminal etale object is an isomorphism.

Let eta be the module adjunction unit and c the abelian adjoint of its underlying abelian morphism. The canonical module-to-abelian inverse-image comparison theorem states that c is an isomorphism. By the adjunction hom equivalence, the abelian unit followed by direct image of c equals the underlying morphism of eta. Evaluate this equality at the terminal etale object. The two factors on the left are isomorphisms, hence so is the forgotten module unit component. This uses exactly the canonical comparison specified by the module unit, not an arbitrary objectwise isomorphism.

The functor forgetting ModuleCat Lambda to AddCommGrpCat reflects isomorphisms (Mathlib isIso_of_reflects_iso). Thus the module unit component is an isomorphism. Compose it with the global-section/terminal-section and terminal-base-change isomorphisms appearing in globalSectionsUpperStarMap. All four factors are isomorphisms, which proves the unchanged statement. This works also for the empty scheme and the zero coefficient ring.
